title: Microdosing: The Low and Slow Approach | House of Zen
h1: Microdosing: The Low and Slow Approach
description: What people mean by microdosing cannabis, how to measure a small THC dose, how long to wait between doses and why we make no promises about the results.
excerpt: Microdosing means a very small, measured amount of THC, taken slowly. Here is how to measure it and how long to wait, without the big promises.
pull: The method is mostly patience, which is the one thing a dispensary cannot sell you.

blocks.html: Microdosing means taking a very small, measured amount of THC rather than a full serving. There is no official definition. Many people use the word for something around 1 to 2.5 mg of THC.

You will find big promises about it elsewhere. We do not make them. We cannot tell you what a small dose will do for you, and neither can anyone else. Some people simply prefer a small, measured amount to a strong one, and going low and slow is a sensible way for any adult to learn how they respond.

Measuring is the hard part, so choose a form that prints its numbers. An edible label gives you the THC in milligrams, and from that you can work out what is in each piece. In Michigan, adult-use edibles are capped at 10 mg of THC per dose and 200 mg per package. That cap is a ceiling, not a target, and a microdose sits well below it.

A small dose may mean cutting one piece into quarters with a clean knife. Be realistic about this. A hand-cut quarter is a rough measure, and labels themselves must state that actual values may vary by 10 percent. A draw from a vaporizer or a pipe has no number printed on it at all.
CBD products are a separate matter. CBD is a different compound, and a CBD product is not a microdose of THC, so read the label for both numbers. Our guide to CBD explains the difference.
These Michigan summaries are general information, not legal advice, as of October 2026.
The method is mostly patience, which is the one thing a dispensary cannot sell you. A simple way to go about it:

items: Choose a day with nothing to drive to and nobody depending on you.
Take the smallest amount you can measure.
Wait at least two hours. Edibles can take that long to arrive, sometimes longer, and a second piece taken early is the classic mistake.
Write down what you took, when you took it and what you noticed.
Keep to the same amount for several sessions before changing anything.

blocks.html: If you notice nothing, that is a perfectly good result. It does not mean you should take more today.

We do not make health claims, and this article is not medical advice. If you take medication, are pregnant or breastfeeding, or have a health condition, talk to your doctor before using cannabis at any dose.
If your reason for trying this has anything to do with your health, that belongs in the same conversation. A doctor can look at your whole picture, and we cannot.

Product education is the part of this work we like best. Bring your questions, and we will go through a label with you and explain what the numbers on it mean. Clear, honest recommendations are a promise of ours, so if we think a low dose plan is more complicated than you need, we will say so.

faq.q: How many milligrams is a microdose?
faq.a_html: There is no official number. Many people use the word for something around 1 to 2.5 mg of THC, but your own starting point is yours to find, slowly.

faq.q: Can I microdose with a vaporizer or flower?
faq.a_html: You can try, but it is harder to measure, because a draw has no number on it. Edibles with a printed dose are easier to keep track of. Our guide to vaporizers covers how they work.
Maybe, maybe not. People differ, and we cannot predict it. If you feel nothing, wait for another day rather than taking more.
